We recognize GenAI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, etc.) are ubiquitous and can help you learn, but your submission must be your own original work. In this course, GenAI is a consulting tool, not an author.

You can carefully use GenAI on assignments, but think of GenAI as a peer in the course. Each assignment will have a section to reflect on your usage of GenAI. You must fill this out to receive credit for the assignment, whether or not you used GenAI or not.

We note that in the past, the single best determinator of students’ exam scores was how well they understood the projects. We advise you to not use GenAI as a shortcut on the projects as this may harm your understanding.

Syllabus CSE 420: Design of Operating Systems Fall 2026
(Clarification: AI tools may be used to support learning, but they may not be used to develop as-
signment solutions. Generating pseudocode, algorithms, implementation plans, or similar solution
components is considered AI assistance on the assignment.)
• I pasted my project code into ChatGPT/Gemini/Copilot/R1/Sonnet/Cursor/OthersSimilar and asked
it to find bugs, explain why my solution was not working, or suggest changes to fix it. (Clarification:
AI tools may not be used to review, debug, modify, improve, or otherwise assist with assignment
solutions. Only the course staff may provide solution-specific debugging assistance.)
• I shared my code publicly on GitHub (or other sites) after the course ended. (Clarification: Sharing
your code after the end of the course is still plagiarism.)
To make it crystal clear, here we provide some AI-specific examples showing what is allowed and
what is not:
• Allowed (These are example learning activities. The AI is acting like a textbook, search en-
gine, tutor, or study guide.):
– What does undefined reference to pthread_create mean?
– Explain how semaphores work.
– Generate 20 multiple-choice questions about deadlocks.
– What is the difference between fork() and exec()?
• Not Allowed (In all of these cases, the AI is contributing directly to the assignment solution,
which must be your own intellectual contribution):
– Here is my Project 2 code (or part of it). Why isn’t it working?
– Here’s my implementation. Fix the race condition.
– Give me pseudocode for implementing this scheduler.
– Design the solution approach for this project.
– Generate the code for the file system traversal.
Please note that AI tools may be used as learning resources but may not be used to generate or
assist in the development of assignment solutions. When in doubt, quickly ask the course instructor
via Teams chat before using an AI tool. Students remain responsible for learning and understand-
ing course material. AI-generated information may be inaccurate, incomplete, or inconsistent with
course content, and course lectures, slides, announcements, and instructor guidance take prece-
dence over information obtained from AI tools.

The use of AI tools like Chat GPT, Claude, Grok, Llama etc. are permitted in this class, however,
you are expected to adhere to the following guidelines to avoid any academic integrity violations:
–Cite any line(s) of code that you use directly from an AI tool.
–Do no use the output of a piece of code directly from an AI tool, you are expected to run the
line(s) of code yourself to generate an output and report that.
–You are still expected to explain the output of any code and comment it to explain what the
line(s) of code are doing whether written by you or generated by an AI tool.
–Also report whether you are using line(s) of code verbatim from an AI tool or you have modiﬁed
the code, clearly identifying the modiﬁcations.
–Do not post the contents of this class including assignments (prose or code) verbatim into any
AI tool or any external website.

Assistance from AI systems such as ChatGPT for writing code or answering homework questions is also strictly prohibited. Please note that AI is likely to produce code similar to that of any other student who uses it. This will get flagged by our plagiarism tools and be treated identically to any other form of copying or plagiarism.

Use of ChatGPT and other AI Writing or Coding Tools in Course Project
The use of AI tools, such as ChatGPT, in course projects is allowed but must adhere to the following
guidelines:
Students are fully responsible for the accuracy and correctness of all content in their submissions,
including any text or code generated by AI. If AI-generated content is incorrect, the assignment will be
graded accordingly. Note that AI is known to output incorrect statements and codes.
Students must disclose their use of AI tools in a visible part of the assignment, such as a code
comment, footnote, or a separate section. The disclosure must clearly identify the AI tool and version

Generative AI tools may not be used for coursework, in any form; the use of such tools (in ideation, summarization, research, feedback, debugging, writing, and/or any other forms of use) is strictly prohibited. The use of a generative AI tool for an assignment constitutes cheating. If you are unsure about whether a particular tool or app uses generative AI, you should ask before using the tool to do classwork.

Students are NOT allowed to use online solutions from previous course offerings,
websites (including ChatGPT), etc. This will be strictly checked and enforced.

This collaboration policy applies equally to recent AI tools such as ChatGPT and other large
language models (LLMs). You are welcome to explore these tools and engage in discussion with
them, but you should not be asking them to solve assignments, and you should not be copying
answers/code from them. Additionally, if you use these tools, you should acknowledge usage and
provide details about how you are using them.

Just LLMing your way through labs is a great way to not learn anything. The labs
are a substantial portion of the grade for a good reason. In systems, clue is
generally gained by doing, not just by “prompt engineering” or “vibe coding” the
latest copyright infringement engine. A competent technical interviewer can detect
a lack of clue very quickly. Don’t make it easy on them.

The use of AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, etc.) is permissible for some activities, including creating and refining study materials, creating outlines for organizing your thoughts or scheduling class activities, or exploring existing APIs for code development. Impermissible uses include generating answers to research questions or reflections, writing technical reports, or making design decisions for homework assignments or the final project. Each of these impermissible uses are core components of the assignments in the course that are designed to help you grow your personal skills in these areas. All uses of AI tools on homeworks or the final project should document in a README file (1) which tool was used, (2) all prompts submitted, and (3) the full output generated by the AI tool.

You are always allowed to use the textbook and any resources provided by me. You are also allowed to use online resources such as StackOverflow, provided that (1) any code taken from other sources is not more than 2-3 lines at a time, (2) the code used does not make up a substantial portion of any part of a lab assignment or single function, and (3) you cite your source with a comment listing the URL from where you found the code. You are not allowed to use any other sources except when specified in the assignment. Plagiarism and cheating, like copying the work of others, paying others to do your work, using code generated by ChatGPT or other AI systems, etc., is prohibited. We will be running MOSS, an automated plagiarism detection tool, on submissions.
